title: Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme at Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3
what_it_is: Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme at Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3

sections.label: First SERS cash top-up
sections.summary: This is the first SERS where selected residents must top up cash for an equivalent replacement flat with a new 99-year lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The key difference is, this is the first time that residents selected for SERS must top up cash to get an equivalent replacement flat with a new 99-year lease.

sections.label: MND memo on West Coast SERS
sections.summary: MND's 14 November memo stated West Coast Road SERS residents who bought equivalent flats received $51,000 for 3-room and $61,000 for 4-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MND finally provided a memo to the Public Petitions Committee on 14 November stating that in a previous SERS at West Coast Road, residents who bought equivalent flats at the "designated" West Coast Crescent site, near their existing flats, had received cash payment from the Government of $51,000 for a 3-room flat and $61,000 for a 4-room flat respectively.

sections.label: Minister's explanation questioned
sections.summary: The Minister did not fully explain why Ang Mo Kio compensation is insufficient, nor why Marsiling SERS residents with 58 to 59 years' lease did not top up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the Minister's explanation does not fully explain why the compensation given to Ang Mo Kio residents is insufficient for them to buy an equivalent flat with a new 99-year lease like in other SERS exercises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: He also did not explain why the residents affected by Marsiling SERS which was announced slightly later than the Ang Mo Kio SERS, did not need to top up with cash although the Marsiling flats have a lease balance of only 58 to 59 years, which is not much longer than the 57 years remaining for the Ang Mo Kio flats.

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio compensation and VERS
sections.summary: The speaker urges improved compensation for Ang Mo Kio residents, reassessment of the Land Acquisition Act, and clarification of future VERS compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has failed to appreciate how stressful and unfair it is to the Ang Mo Kio residents, for them to fork out tens of thousands of dollars to move to a new location, forced upon them by national development needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to further improve the compensation package for the Ang Mo Kio residents, although a final compensation has been announced on 7 November last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fifty years after the introduction of the Land Acquisition Act, it is time for us to reassess the Act with regards to its power, to displace Singaporeans from their homes without adequate compensation for them to afford an equivalent replacement home in the same area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singaporeans, especially those who live in older flats with decaying leases, should be aware that the Ang Mo Kio SERS possibly foreshadowed what could happen to them in the future if the Government uses the compensation formula applied to the Ang Mo Kio SERS for VERS in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to clarify how it intends to compensate the residents of VERS in the future, because Singaporeans needs certainty on the lease decay issue as soon as possible.

sections.label: SERS compensation not pegged
sections.summary: SERS compensation has never been intentionally pegged to the price of a new flat of similar size and location on a fresh 99-year lease.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: First of all, SERS compensation has never been intentionally pegged to the price of a new flat of similar size, in a similar location, on a fresh 99-year lease.

sections.label: Flexibility and 99% no top-up
sections.summary: After listening to residents and Ms Nadia Samdin's representations, flexibility was introduced so 99% of flat owners need not top up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: While we have maintained our approach towards the valuation of flats, we have also introduced flexibility after listening from the residents, and also the representations of their representative, Ms Nadia Samdin.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: And as a result of that, 99% of flat owners need not top up to purchase a similar type of flat with a full 99-year lease or a similar sized flat on a 50-year lease.

sections.label: VERS terms not announced
sections.summary: VERS details are unannounced, and the Government says its terms will be less generous than SERS with no replacement flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The details of VERS have yet to be announced but the Government has already made clear that the terms for VERS will not be as generous as for SERS and that there are no replacement flats.

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio threshold claim
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Leong characterises Ang Mo Kio as a crossed threshold and blurs market expectation with policy commitment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In his speech, he characterises what has happened in Ang Mo Kio as some threshold having been crossed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: And I think what Mr Leong is doing here is blurring the distinction between a market expectation and a policy commitment.

sections.label: Government denies being disingenuous
sections.summary: The speaker rejects claims the Government was disingenuous or non-transparent, saying Mr Leong blurs market expectation and policy commitment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But this cannot be the case for all SERS exercises, and we have explained that.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: So, I think that far from the Government being disingenuous, far from the Government having been non-transparent or non-empathetic to ground concerns, I would put it, Mr Speaker, to the House that it is Mr Leong who is being disingenuous in blurring the distinction between a market expectation and a policy commitment, and also shaping expectations of a policy whose parameters we have given some outline to, but he has shaped it the other way.

sections.label: Upcoming debate on schemes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Mr Leong will engage responsibly in the upcoming debate instead of conflating issues and shaping ungrounded expectations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I also believe that we will have an opportunity to debate fully in this House on these matters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But I hope that instead of conflating issues, confusing issues or quite deliberately misleading the public by shaping ungrounded expectations of schemes, creating goalposts as it were, I hope that Mr Leong will engage in the upcoming debate responsibly.

sections.label: VERS and Ang Mo Kio SERS
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether VERS compensation will be unattractive if analogised to Ang Mo Kio SERS, noting SERS sites are limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Even before, with this Ang Mo Kio SERS incident which points to the fact that the compensation would be very different – of course, the guidelines for VERS have not been totally clear or announced at the moment – but does the Senior Minister of State agree that if we draw an analogy of VERS with the Ang Mo Kio SERS exercise, then the VERS compensation will not be attractive to Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have said more than once that the selection of sites for SERS necessarily has to be limited, that only about 5% of sites could be suitable for SERS and that, in fact, many suitable sites have already gone through the exercise.

sections.label: Government upfront on leases
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government has been upfront about diminishing leases and the relativity between VERS and SERS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: With regard to diminishing leases, again the Government has also been upfront in letting residents know about this, in being clear to home owners in terms of the relativity between VERS and SERS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: If Mr Leong takes a look at our article on Gov.sg, I think it cannot possibly be clearer.
